database_summary: A small music store schema (Chinook-like) in SQLite containing artists, albums, tracks, media types and genres as the catalog; customers, employees as people; invoices and invoice_items as sales transactions; playlists and playlist_track as user-curated lists. Row counts indicate a catalog of ~3.5k tracks, ~350 albums and modest sales (~412 invoices, 2.2k invoice lines). Foreign keys model straightforward relationships (e.g., tracks->albums->artists, invoice_items->invoices->customers).

accepted.name: tracks_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  tracks.TrackId AS TrackId,
  tracks.Name AS Name,
  tracks.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  albums.Title AS Title,
  albums.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  artists.Name AS Name_Artist,
  tracks.MediaTypeId AS MediaTypeId,
  media_types.Name AS Name_MediaType,
  tracks.GenreId AS GenreId,
  genres.Name AS Name_Genre,
  tracks.Composer AS Composer,
  tracks.Milliseconds AS Milliseconds,
  tracks.Bytes AS Bytes,
  tracks.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice
FROM tracks
LEFT JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ON albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN media_types ON tracks.MediaTypeId = media_types.MediaTypeId
LEFT JOIN genres ON tracks.GenreId = genres.GenreId
accepted.description: Denormalized track-level catalog: one row per TrackId with track attributes plus album title and artist name, genre name and media type name. Use this as a canonical track catalog for filtering, aggregation, or joining to sales and playlists. | Use for: List tracks with artist/album/genre/media labels; Aggregate track counts or durations by artist/genre/media type; Filter tracks by composer, duration, size, or price before joining to sales or playlists

accepted.name: invoice_lines_enriched
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  invoice_items.InvoiceLineId AS InvoiceLineId,
  invoice_items.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  invoices.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  invoices.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  invoices.BillingCountry AS BillingCountry,
  invoice_items.TrackId AS TrackId,
  invoice_items.UnitPrice AS UnitPrice,
  invoice_items.Quantity AS Quantity,
  (invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity) AS LineAmount,
  tracks.TrackId AS TrackId_Track,
  tracks.Name AS Name,
  tracks.AlbumId AS AlbumId,
  albums.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  artists.Name AS Name_Artist,
  tracks.GenreId AS GenreId,
  genres.Name AS Name_Genre
FROM invoice_items
LEFT JOIN invoices ON invoice_items.InvoiceId = invoices.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks ON invoice_items.TrackId = tracks.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ON albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId
LEFT JOIN genres ON tracks.GenreId = genres.GenreId
accepted.description: Denormalized invoice line items: one row per InvoiceLineId including invoice header info, customer id and invoice date, plus track metadata (via tracks_enriched). Useful for sales analysis at the line level and for joining revenue to track/artist/genre. | Use for: Compute revenue or units sold by track/artist/genre over time; Identify top-selling tracks or artists; Analyze customer purchases by country or customer

accepted.name: customer_summary
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  customers.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  customers.FirstName AS FirstName,
  customers.LastName AS LastName,
  COUNT(DISTINCT invoices.InvoiceId) AS InvoiceCount,
  SUM(invoices.Total) AS TotalSpent,
  COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId) AS DistinctTracksPurchased,
  MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate) AS LastInvoiceDate
FROM customers
LEFT JOIN invoices ON customers.CustomerId = invoices.CustomerId
LEFT JOIN invoice_items ON invoices.InvoiceId = invoice_items.InvoiceId
GROUP BY customers.CustomerId, customers.FirstName, customers.LastName
accepted.description: Per-customer aggregates derived from invoices and invoice_items: total spent, number of invoices, number of distinct tracks purchased, and last invoice date. Useful for customer lifetime value, recency/frequency/monetary analyses and customer segmentation. | Use for: Rank customers by total spend or invoice frequency; Identify inactive customers by LastInvoiceDate; Feed RFM segmentation or churn prediction features

accepted.name: artist_sales_agg
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  artists.ArtistId AS ArtistId,
  artists.Name AS Name,
  SUM(invoice_items.UnitPrice * invoice_items.Quantity) AS Revenue,
  SUM(invoice_items.Quantity) AS QuantitySold,
  COUNT(DISTINCT invoice_items.TrackId) AS DistinctTracksSold,
  MIN(invoices.InvoiceDate) AS FirstSaleDate,
  MAX(invoices.InvoiceDate) AS LastSaleDate
FROM invoice_items
LEFT JOIN invoices ON invoice_items.InvoiceId = invoices.InvoiceId
LEFT JOIN tracks ON invoice_items.TrackId = tracks.TrackId
LEFT JOIN albums ON tracks.AlbumId = albums.AlbumId
LEFT JOIN artists ON albums.ArtistId = artists.ArtistId
GROUP BY artists.ArtistId, artists.Name
accepted.description: Artist-level sales aggregates computed from invoice lines joined to track->album->artist: total revenue, total quantity sold, distinct tracks sold, and first/last sale date per artist. Useful for comparing artist performance over time. | Use for: List top-earning artists; Track revenue trajectory per artist between dates; Compare quantity vs revenue across artists

accepted.name: track_popularity_rank
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  t.TrackId AS TrackId,
  t.Name AS Name,
  COALESCE(SUM(ii.Quantity), 0) AS QuantitySold,
  COALESCE(SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity), 0) AS Revenue,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(ii.Quantity),0) DESC) AS QuantityRank,
  RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(SUM(ii.UnitPrice * ii.Quantity),0) DESC) AS RevenueRank
FROM tracks t
LEFT JOIN invoice_items ii ON t.TrackId = ii.TrackId
GROUP BY t.TrackId, t.Name
ORDER BY Revenue DESC
accepted.description: Ranked tracks by sales volume and revenue: one row per TrackId with total quantity and revenue and rank columns that order tracks by QuantitySold and Revenue (ties handled by RANK). Useful as a basis for Top-K queries by applying WHERE QuantityRank <= k or RevenueRank <= k downstream. | Use for: Return top-N tracks by units sold or revenue; Compare rank positions across different metrics; Filter top tracks within a genre/artist by joining to tracks_enriched

accepted.name: playlist_track_counts
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  p.PlaylistId AS PlaylistId,
  p.Name AS Name,
  COUNT(pt.TrackId) AS TrackCount,
  SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS TotalMilliseconds,
  SUM(t.Bytes) AS TotalBytes
FROM playlists p
LEFT JOIN playlist_track pt ON p.PlaylistId = pt.PlaylistId
LEFT JOIN tracks t ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
GROUP BY p.PlaylistId, p.Name
accepted.description: Per-playlist counts and total duration: one row per PlaylistId giving number of tracks and total milliseconds and total bytes. Useful to rank or filter playlists by size or duration and to join with playlist metadata. | Use for: Find largest or longest playlists; Filter playlists by minimum total duration or track count; Compare playlist sizes across names

accepted.name: invoices_with_customer
accepted.body_sql:
SELECT
  invoices.InvoiceId AS InvoiceId,
  invoices.CustomerId AS CustomerId,
  customers.FirstName AS FirstName,
  customers.LastName AS LastName,
  customers.Email AS Email,
  invoices.InvoiceDate AS InvoiceDate,
  invoices.BillingCountry AS BillingCountry,
  invoices.Total AS Total
FROM invoices
LEFT JOIN customers ON invoices.CustomerId = customers.CustomerId
accepted.description: Invoice header joined with customer basic info: one row per InvoiceId containing billing fields and customer contact, for use in customer-level or invoice-level reporting. | Use for: Invoice lists with customer contact for outreach; Aggregate invoice totals by country or customer; Filter invoices by date ranges or customer attributes
